title: Two-pole/simplex upper bound on any universal boundary constant
statement: For the singular correlation family with two identical poles, k regular-simplex ring points, pole-ring correlation a, and distinct-ring correlation (k a^2-1)/(k-1), the pole-difference coefficient converges at fixed 0<a<1 to 1+1/(2-a^2) as k tends to infinity. Consequently no dimension-uniform inequality K0(C)>=c P_ker(C) can hold for c>3/2.
assumptions: The limit k to infinity is taken at fixed positive a before a tends to zero
K0 is the average of M_pi^{-T} M_pi^{-1} with the lower-in-order convention
open_objections: This is only an upper bound on the best possible universal constant; it does not prove K0(C)>=(3/2)P_ker(C).
It does not prove that any positive dimension-uniform constant exists.
No Lean formalization, priority audit, or outside-human validation exists.
